abstract.t: This document specifies the X-Forwarded-Prefix HTTP header field, a widely deployed de-facto standard used by reverse proxies, API gateways, load balancers, and ingress controllers to communicate the original URI path prefix that was stripped, rewritten, or matched prior to forwarding a request to an upstream service. Standardizing this header provides normative behavior across HTTP intermediaries and origin servers, enabling upstream applications to reliably reconstruct original client-facing target URIs, issue accurate HTTP redirects, generate self-referential hypermedia links, configure application base paths, and mitigate security vulnerabilities arising from improper path handling and header injection. Furthermore, this document establishes the requirement for reverse proxy implementations to emit this header unless explicitly configured otherwise, specifies deterministic prefix concatenation for multi- proxy chaining, defines strict percent-encoding preservation, establishes atomic trust boundaries for the forwarded header family, specifies structured field mapping in accordance with RFC 9651, and registers the field in the IANA HTTP Field Name Registry along with an extension parameter for the RFC 7239 Forwarded header.
